# Hevatthikathā (Kv 1.10)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Hevatthikathā* ("Debate on 'It Exists Thus'") is the tenth discourse of the first chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The debate centers on the proposition that phenomena exist only in a specific manner (*evatthi* / *hevatthi*) and not otherwise [Dube 1980]. According to modern scholarship, this controversy addresses a thesis attributed to the Andhakas (including the Pubbaseliyas) holding that the past, present, and future exist strictly as past, present, and future respectively, rather than otherwise [Dube 1980]. The Theravādins criticize this formulation on the grounds that it inadvertently predicates both existence and non-existence to the same phenomenon [Dube 1980]. The dialectical exchange contrasting *hevatthi* and *hevanatthi* against the Theravādin positions (*sevatthi* and *sevanatthi*) has been noted for its formal resemblance to the Jain doctrine of conditional predication (*saptabhaṅgīnaya*) [Dube 1980].
SuttaCentral registers one modern translation and lists no curated cross-linguistic parallels [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal text reuse across 23 Pali texts (870 matching passages), sharing extensive phrasing with related temporal debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, notably the *Ekaccaṁatthītikathā* (Kv 1.8), the *Atītakkhandhādikathā* (Kv 1.7), and the *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), as well as the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), and commentary literature including the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-anuṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also generates machine-level cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (Taishō 99) [DharmaNexus].
